transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-20 15:00 PST / Duration: ~42 mins
Attendees: Ari Nguyen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (Head of ML - Cloudcrest), Maya Ortiz (Platform Eng), Liam Chen (CTO)

Summary: Quick console walkthrough focusing on per-route usage analytics, per-route cost breakdowns, and how Redwood Optimize recommendations reduce unit cost. Customer interested in hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, VPC connectivity, and SOC2 controls. Agreed next steps for pricing and a benchmark pilot.

Topics: console overview, per-route dashboards, token-level cost, routing policies, batching/quantization suggestions, security docs, pilot timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Ari: All right thanks everyone for joining, this is Ari from Redwood, today Samira and I will walk through the Console usage analytics and cost breakdowns - hi Jared, hi Maya, hi Liam.
[00:12] Jared: Hey thanks for doing this, we've been poking around the API but want to see the console side for ops and cost visibility.
[00:20] Samira: Great - we'll jump in. Quick note, if anything is unclear interrupt, we can zoom into the Dedicated or VPC parts later.
[00:30] Ari: K, starting on the console home - you can see top-level spend, tokens, requests by model, and per-route. The per-route dashboards are what most ops teams use to attribute cost to product features.
[00:48] Maya: Quick q: how granular is the token cost? Like can we map embeddings vs chat generation and tie to a route?
[00:55] Samira: Yes, it's token-level; we break down by input vs output and by model variant. Routes map to API keys or path so you can filter by service. There's also per-token latency percentiles.
[01:12] Liam: And this works for Dedicated too? We need to understand committed capacity economics first.
[01:18] Ari: Yep; console shows both hosted and dedicated usage. For Dedicated you'll see reserved capacity utilization metrics and a forecast for when you'll hit commit. We also show a cost delta comparing hosted vs reserved to help decide.
[01:33] Jared: We're sensitive to latency: checkout flow needs <200ms 95p. Can Redwood guarantee that on hosted?
[01:40] Samira: Hosted has SLO tiers; depends on model and token lengths. For strict p95 latency we usually recommend Dedicated or a smaller model variant pinned for that route, plus prefix caching.
[01:51] Jared: Makes sense. Also curious about Optimize recommendations - how prescriptive are they?
[01:57] Samira: Optimize suggests batching, cache TTLs, model quantization options, and route-level routing policies (e.g., route X uses model-a for low latency, fall back to model-b for cost). Suggestions come with estimated cost savings and expected latency impact.
[02:14] Ari: I'm going to open the per-route dashboard for your checkout route example - note the breakdown: tokens, calls, avg latency, 95/99p, cost per 1k tokens, and inferred model mix.
[02:30] Maya: I see a spike on Nov 3 - what is that?
[02:33] Samira: That was a misattributed batch job hitting the route; console highlights anomalies and ties them to IPs or API keys when possible.
[02:41] Jared: Security - do you retain logs? We need audit logs plus KMS integration.
[02:46] Ari: Yes, we have audit logs, VPC/private deployment options, and KMS/HSM integrations. I'll share the SOC2 and security bundle after the call (link in next steps). For hosted we retain request metadata for X days by default, adjustable for enterprise customers.
[03:02] Liam: What's the process for Private deployment? We are regulated in EU so might need VPC or on-prem.
[03:08] Samira: Private deployment is a separate package, includes a customer-managed control plane and connectors for your KMS. On-prem requires field engineering coordination for air-gapped installs. Timeline is typically 6-10 weeks depending on network and infra.
[03:22] Jared: Can we run a quick benchmark with our dataset to confirm quality and latency?
[03:27] Ari: Absolutely - typical pilot is 2 weeks: you provide a sample dataset, we run throughput/latency tests and produce a per-route cost estimate. Samira will coordinate.
[03:36] Samira: I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet template - it has traffic profiles, seq length distributions, and sample prompts. Also include expected RPS and SLOs.
[03:45] Maya: On the cost model - how do you handle caching savings? If we do prefix caching, how is that shown?
[03:51] Samira: The console shows effective token reductions from cache hits and model reuse; Optimize simulates different cache TTLs and shows savings. We also show CPU/GPU utilization on Dedicated so you can see headroom for burst traffic.
[04:07] Ari: I'll demo a recent customer's dashboard - imagine route "checkout/price-quote" - you can group by model, by API key, or by feature flag. There's a toggle to break costs into model cost vs infra overhead vs caching benefit.
[04:23] Jared: Do you provide alerts for cost regressions?
[04:26] Samira: Yes, cost/regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals. You can set thresholds per route and get notified in Slack or email.
[04:35] Liam: Any integrations for our internal observability - we use Datadog and Sentry.
[04:39] Ari: We have tracing hooks and a Datadog exporter; we can push metrics or provide a private endpoint for ingestion.
[04:46] Jared: Competitors question - we looked at VendorX; their dashboard skews simple. How is Redwood different?
[04:52] Samira: We're production-first: granular per-route economics, routing policies, and built-in fallbacks. Plus Optimize recommendations are workload-aware and tied to actual runes - er, runtime metrics.
[05:05] Jared: Ha, runes - runtime metrics, yes - transcription typo there.
[05:10] Samira: (laughs) classic transcription.
[05:12] Ari: Going into the cost breakdown tab - you can select time window and the console slices cost by route and model. It shows the cost per 1k tokens and also an amortized infra cost for Dedicated pools.
[05:25] Maya: How accurate is the infra amortization? If we have GPUs on-prem it's different.
[05:29] Ari: For on-prem/Dedicated we use actual pool sizing and your committed rate; for hosted it's based on our cost model which we disclose in the pricing doc. We can also upload your instance pricing so amortization matches your internal costs.
[05:43] Jared: Any recommendations for our high-volume search reranking route? It's very latency sensitive but tolerant of slightly lower quality if cost savings big.
[05:51] Samira: For reranking we often suggest a two-stage pipeline: cheap embeddings + small reranker for first pass and heavy reranker only for top-K. Optimize can recommend quantized model variants for the reranker to reduce token cost.
[06:05] Ari: We're hitting about 20 minutes of content; quick recap of action items and next steps.
[06:12] Jared: Couple final Qs: billing granularity? and SLA?
[06:16] Ari: Billing is per-token and per-embedding unit on hosted; Dedicated has commit + overage pricing. SLA varies by offering; Dedicated includes uptime SLA and latency targets in enterprise contracts. We'll share the sample contract.
[06:27] Samira: I'll set up the benchmark, share the template and we'll include an example dashboard export so you can see the exact fields.
[06:35] Maya: Perfect. One ask - can you send an example of the per-route policy config (json/yaml)?
[06:41] Samira: Yes, I'll include a snippet in the follow-up.
[06:44] Ari: Ok thanks everyone - we'll follow up with pricing, SOC2 bundle (https://redwood.ai/security), and the benchmark template (shared drive link).
[06:54] Jared: Thanks, talk soon.

Recap & Next Steps (spoken):
- Redwood: Send pricing & committed capacity options, SOC2 + security docs, benchmark template.
